``` {r FUNCTIONS}
# Create all Functions necessary for Report

### Filter Functions ###
# Survey
FilterFunction1 <- function(data) {
  data %>% 
    mutate(TripDate = as.Date(substring(QuadratID, 8, 15), format = "%Y%m%d"),
           FixedLocationID = substring(QuadratID, 19, 22),
           Year = year(TripDate)) %>%
    left_join(FixedLocations1, by = c("FixedLocationID")) %>%
    mutate(TimeSinceCultched = as.numeric(interval(DateLastCultched, TripDate), "years")) %>%
    mutate(ProjectGroup = case_when(
      grepl("RESTORE", StationName) ~ "RESTORE-2017",
      grepl("NFWF", StationName) & Year < 2019 ~ "NFWF-2015",
      grepl("SBM Hotel", StationName) | grepl("SBM Bulkhead", StationName) ~ "Historic Uncultched",
      grepl("SBM", StationName) & Year >= 2021 & TimeSinceCultched > 0 ~ "NFWF-2021",
      grepl("NFWF21", StationName) ~ "NFWF-2021",
      grepl("NFWF24-25", StationName) | grepl("NFWF24-26", StationName) ~ "NFWF-2024 General",
      grepl("NFWF24", StationName) ~ "NFWF-2024 Pilot",
      grepl("Intertidal", ParcelName) ~ "Intertidal",
      TRUE ~ "Historic Uncultched")) 
}
###

### Survey Functions ###
summarise_ALL <- function(data) {
  summarised_data <- data %>%
    summarise(NumLiveMean_raw = mean(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
              NumLiveSD_raw = sd(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
              NumDrillsMean_raw = mean(NumDrills, na.rm = TRUE),
              NumDrillsSD_raw = sd(NumDrills, na.rm = TRUE),
              NumLegalMean_raw = mean(NumLegal, na.rm = TRUE),
              NumLegalSD_raw = sd(NumLegal, na.rm = TRUE),
              TotalWeightMean_raw = mean(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
              TotalWeightSD_raw = sd(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE)) %>%
    mutate(NumLiveDensityMean_raw = NumLiveMean_raw * 4,
           NumLiveDensitySD_raw = NumLiveSD_raw * 4,
           NumDrillDensityMean_raw = NumDrillsMean_raw * 4,
           NumDrillDensitySD_raw = NumDrillsSD_raw * 4,
           NumLegalDensityMean_raw = NumLegalMean_raw * 4,
           NumLegalDensitySD_raw = NumLegalSD_raw * 4,
           TotalWeightDensityMean_raw = TotalWeightMean_raw * 4,
           TotalWeightDensitySD_raw = TotalWeightSD_raw * 4)
  return(summarised_data)
}

###

### Plot Functions
  # Function to generate grouped bar plots with SD bars
  # df is short for data frame
generate_grouped_plot <- function(df, x_variable, x_label, y_variable, y_label, y_SD, UseColor, UseFill, title) {
  
  df <- df %>%
    mutate(Upper = !!sym(y_variable) + !!sym(y_SD))
  max_upper <- max(ungroup(df) %>%
                     dplyr::select(Upper), na.rm = TRUE)
  
  plot_list <- df %>% 
    ggplot(aes(x = factor(!!sym(x_variable), levels = unique(!!sym(x_variable))), 
               y = !!sym(y_variable), 
               color = !!sym(UseColor), 
               fill = as.factor(!!sym(UseFill)))) + 
    geom_bar(stat = "identity", 
             position = position_dodge(width = 0.9),
             color = "black") + 
    geom_errorbar(aes(ymin = !!sym(y_variable), ymax = Upper), 
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.9), 
                  width = 0.25, color = "black") + 
    scale_x_discrete(x_label, expand = c(0.005, 0), 
                     guide = guide_axis(angle = -45)) +
    scale_y_continuous(y_label, expand = c(0, 0),
                       limits = c(0, ceiling(max_upper * 1.05)),
                       breaks = pretty(0:2 * ceiling(max(ungroup(df) %>% 
                                                           dplyr::select(Upper), na.rm = TRUE) / 2))) + 
    ggtitle(title) + 
    BaseForm +
    theme(legend.position = "bottom",
          plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0, vjust = 0)) 
  
  return(plot_list)
}
```

```{r DatabaseDownload}
# Load Database Data
# Connect to Local database server and pull all necessary data, then close connection 
con <- dbConnect(odbc(),
                 Driver = "SQL Server", 
                 Server = Server,
                 Database = Database,
                 Authentication = "ActiveDirectoryIntegrated")

# Load Fixed location information
dboFixedLocations <- tbl(con,in_schema("dbo", "FixedLocations")) %>%
  collect() %>% 
  filter(Estuary %in% Estuaries)

# Load Survey Data
hsdbSurveyQuadrat <- tbl(con,in_schema("hsdb", "SurveyQuadrat")) %>%
  collect() %>%
  filter(substring(SampleEventID, 1, 2) %in% Estuaries)

hsdbSurveySH <- tbl(con,in_schema("hsdb", "SurveySH")) %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate(ShellHeight = as.integer(ShellHeight)) %>%
  filter(substring(QuadratID, 1, 2) %in% Estuaries)

hsdbShellBudgetQuadrat <- tbl(con,in_schema("hsdb", "ShellBudgetQuadrat")) %>%
  collect() %>%
  filter(substring(SampleEventID, 1, 2) %in% Estuaries)

hsdbShellBudgetSH <- tbl(con,in_schema("hsdb", "ShellBudgetSH")) %>%
  collect() %>%
  mutate(ShellHeight = as.integer(ShellHeight)) %>%
  filter(substring(QuadratID, 1, 2) %in% Estuaries)

# Disconnect from database
DBI::dbDisconnect(con)

# Remove connection
rm(con)
```

``` {r BasicFilters}
# Filter data frames so that only data collected for inclusion in the Report are present.

### Location Data ###
FixedLocations1 <- dboFixedLocations %>% 
  mutate(StationNumber = as.numeric(StationNumber),

         StationNumber,

         CultchDensity,

    ### Remove intermediate data frames
rm(dboFixedLocations)

######
### Survey Data ###
    ### QUADRATS ###

Survey_Quad1 <- hsdbSurveyQuadrat %>%
  select(QuadratID,
         SampleEventID,
         NumLive,

  FilterFunction1() %>%

         NumDead,
         NumDrills,
         NumLegal,
         TotalWeight,
         Comments) %>%
  filter(Year == 2026,
         StationNumber > 500)
    ###

    # Shell Budget QUADRATS #
SBM_Quad1 <- hsdbShellBudgetQuadrat %>%
  rename(TotalWeight = TotalSampleWeight, # Must rename the columns so we can union them together
         NumLive = NumLiveOysters,
         NumDead = NumDeadOysters) %>%
  mutate(NumLegal = NA) %>% # This column doesn't occur in that table, but needs to exist to union
  select(QuadratID,

  FilterFunction1() %>%
```

``` {r BasicStats}
### Set Project Group order to display
ProjectGroupOrder <- c("NFWF-2021", "NFWF-2024", "NFWF-2024 Pilot", "NFWF-2024 General", "NFWF-2024 General Adjusted",
                       "Pilot HIGH", "Pilot LOW", "General", "General Adjusted")
QuadStats0 <- Quadrats_ALL %>%
  mutate(NumALLOys = NumLive + NumDead,
         DLRatio = NumDead / NumLive) %>%
    mutate(Treatment = case_when(
      ProjectGroup == "NFWF-2021" ~ "NFWF-2021",
      StationNumber == 525 ~ "NFWF-2024-Cat-Point",
      StationNumber == 526 ~ "NFWF-2024-Easthole",
      CultchDensity == 1600 ~ "Low-Relief",
      CultchDensity == 3200 ~ "High-Relief",
      TRUE ~ "ERROR")) %>%
  # remove erroneous samples from NFWF-2024 General where sampling occurred where no cultching had occurred
  filter(!str_detect(QuadratID, "ABSRVY_20260613_1_0525_1"))
ShellHeights_1 <- ShellHeights_ALL %>%
  # remove erroneous samples from NFWF-2024 General where sampling occurred where no cultching had occurred
  filter(!str_detect(QuadratID, "ABSRVY_20260613_1_0525_1")) 

# Prep data frame for creating SH distribution histogram 
ShellHeights_2 <- ShellHeights_1 %>%
  filter(!is.na(ShellHeight)) %>%
  mutate(Treatment = case_when(
      ProjectGroup == "NFWF-2021" ~ "NFWF-2021",
      StationNumber == 525 ~ "NFWF-2024-Cat-Point",
      StationNumber == 526 ~ "NFWF-2024-Easthole",
      CultchDensity == 1600 ~ "Low-Relief",
      CultchDensity == 3200 ~ "High-Relief",
      TRUE ~ "ERROR")) %>%
  mutate(ShellHeightBin = cut(ShellHeight, 
                              breaks = seq(0, ceiling(max(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE)) + 5, by = 5),
                              right = TRUE,
                              include.lowest = TRUE)) %>% # puts measures in 5 mm bins
  group_by(Treatment) %>%
  mutate(ProjectTotal = n()) %>%
  group_by(Treatment, ShellHeightBin, ProjectTotal) %>%
  summarise(ProjectNumberMeasured = n()) %>%
  mutate(PercentMeasured = (ProjectNumberMeasured / ProjectTotal) * 100)

# Determine number of oysters measured during ReportYear
ShellHeightsReportYr <- ShellHeights_1 %>%
  filter(!is.na(ShellHeight)) 
# Determine size of largest oyster measure during ReportYear 
maxSH <- max(ShellHeightsReportYr$ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE)

```

``` {r NFWF-2021 NumLegal calculation}
# NumLegal wasn't recorded, so we must extrapolate based on SH measures
### Provides how many were measured for each size class for each quadrat
SHMeasures <- ShellHeights_1 %>%
  filter(ProjectGroup == "NFWF-2021") %>%
  group_by(QuadratID) %>%
  summarize(TotalNumMeasured = sum(!is.na(ShellHeight)),
            Count_Legal_76_plus = sum(ifelse(ShellHeight >= 76, 1, 0), na.rm = TRUE)
  )

### Provide stats for how many live oysters there were in each quadrat, by size class
LegalMeasures <- left_join(QuadStats0, SHMeasures, by = c("QuadratID")) %>%
  mutate(
    Num_Legal_76_plus = if_else(TotalNumMeasured == 0, 0, (Count_Legal_76_plus * NumLive) / TotalNumMeasured)) %>%
  select(-starts_with("Count_")) # Remove Count columns as they are no longer needed

QuadStats <- LegalMeasures %>%
  mutate(NumLegal = round(if_else(is.na(NumLegal), Num_Legal_76_plus, NumLegal))) 
  
# Remove intermediate data frames
rm(LegalMeasures, SHMeasures, QuadStats0)
```


``` {r NFWF-2024 General Explore, eval = FALSE}
# Exploring the NFWF-2024 General data to see if TotalWeight, NumLive, NumALLOys, and ShellHeight data was affected by the 2026 Easthole Mortality Event.
### 
# Findings: TotalWeight differences were significant, but just barely, so will be treated together. NumLive differences were NOT significant, so will be treated together. NumALLOys differences were HIGHLY significant, so will not be treated together. ShellHeight differences were HIGHLY significant, so will not be treated together.
###

# Filter data frames for basic stats
Qexplore <- QuadStats %>%
  filter(ProjectGroup == "NFWF-2024 General")
SHexplore <- ShellHeights_1 %>%
  filter(ProjectGroup == "NFWF-2024 General")

# Weight, Live, ALL Summary by station name and Overall
TWstation_summary <- Qexplore %>%
  group_by(StationName) %>%
  summarise(
    meanTW   = mean(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_TW    = sd(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    medianTW = median(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    maxTW    = max(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    minTW    = min(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    meanNL   = mean(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_NL    = sd(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    medianNL = median(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    maxNL    = max(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    minNL    = min(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
        meanALL   = mean(NumALLOys, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_ALL    = sd(NumALLOys, na.rm = TRUE),
    medianALL = median(NumALLOys, na.rm = TRUE),
    maxALL    = max(NumALLOys, na.rm = TRUE),
    minALL    = min(NumALLOys, na.rm = TRUE))
              
TWoverall_summary <- Qexplore %>%
  summarise(
    StationName = "Overall",
    meanTW   = mean(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_TW    = sd(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    medianTW = median(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    maxTW    = max(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    minTW    = min(TotalWeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    meanNL   = mean(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_NL    = sd(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    medianNL = median(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    maxNL    = max(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    minNL    = min(NumLive, na.rm = TRUE),
    meanALL   = mean(NumALLOys, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_ALL    = sd(NumALLOys, na.rm = TRUE),
    medianALL = median(NumALLOys, na.rm = TRUE),
    maxALL    = max(NumALLOys, na.rm = TRUE),
    minALL    = min(NumALLOys, na.rm = TRUE))

# Combine both summaries into one table
TW_report <- bind_rows(TWstation_summary, TWoverall_summary)

# ShellHeight Summary by station name
SHstation_summary <- SHexplore %>%
  group_by(StationName) %>%
  summarise(
    meanSH   = mean(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_SH    = sd(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    medianSH = median(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    maxSH    = max(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    minSH    = min(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE))
              
SHoverall_summary <- SHexplore %>%
  summarise(
    StationName = "Overall",
    meanSH   = mean(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    sd_SH    = sd(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    medianSH = median(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    maxSH    = max(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE),
    minSH    = min(ShellHeight, na.rm = TRUE))

# Combine both summaries into one table
SH_report <- bind_rows(SHstation_summary, SHoverall_summary)

# Combine both reports into a single FINAL Report & delete intermediate
FINAL_report_NFWF2024General <- left_join(TW_report, SH_report, by = "StationName")
rm(TWstation_summary, TWoverall_summary, TW_report, SHstation_summary, SHoverall_summary, SH_report)

# Determine if Cat Point and Easthole data is statistically different
# Total Weight
# Check if variances are equal
var_testTW <- var.test(TotalWeight ~ StationName, data = Qexplore)
print(var_testTW)
# Since variances are equal (p = 0.433), perform t-test
t_test_equalTW <- t.test(TotalWeight ~ StationName, data = Qexplore, var.equal = TRUE)
print(t_test_equalTW)
# p = 0.044, which is statistically significant, but just barely, no data filtering needed

# NumLive
# Check if variances are equal
var_testNL <- var.test(NumLive ~ StationName, data = Qexplore)
print(var_testNL)
# Since variances are equal (p = 0.191), perform t-test
t_test_equalNL <- t.test(NumLive ~ StationName, data = Qexplore, var.equal = TRUE)
print(t_test_equalNL)
# p = 0.931, which is NOT statistically significant, no data filtering needed

# NumALLOys
# Check if variances are equal
var_testALL <- var.test(NumALLOys ~ StationName, data = Qexplore)
print(var_testALL)
# Since variances are equal (p = 0.958), perform t-test
t_test_equalALL <- t.test(NumALLOys ~ StationName, data = Qexplore, var.equal = TRUE)
print(t_test_equalALL)
# p < 0.001, which is HIGHLY statistically significant, These should not be treated together

# SH
# Check if variances are equal
var_testSH <- var.test(ShellHeight ~ StationName, data = SHexplore)
print(var_testSH)
# Since variances ARE NOT equal (p < 0.001), perform Welch's t-test, which is the safer default in R
t_test_welchSH <- t.test(ShellHeight ~ StationName, data = SHexplore, var.equal = FALSE)
print(t_test_welchSH)
# p < 0.001, which is HIGHLY statistically significant, These should not be treated together
```

``` {r TotalWeight Model selection, eval = FALSE}
# Figure out which data distribution to use
# ALL
hist(QuadStats$TotalWeight) 
# normal, range 0 - 30, strong peak at 12;

# NFWF-2021
hist(subset(QuadStats, str_detect(ProjectGroup, "NFWF-2021"))$TotalWeight) 
# normal, range 2 - 16, strong peak at 9; 

# NFWF-2024 All
hist(subset(QuadStats, str_detect(ProjectGroup, "NFWF-2024"))$TotalWeight) 
# normal, range 0 - 30, strong peak at 12; 

# NFWF-2024 General
hist(subset(QuadStats, ProjectGroup == "NFWF-2024 General")$TotalWeight) 
# normal, range 5 - 20, strong peak at 14; 

# NFWF-2024 Pilot
hist(subset(QuadStats, ProjectGroup == "NFWF-2024 Pilot")$TotalWeight) 
# normal, range 0 - 30, peak at 12

# Pilot HIGH
hist(subset(QuadStats, CultchDensity == 3200)$TotalWeight)
# normal, range 5 - 30, peak at 12

# Pilot LOW
hist(subset(QuadStats, CultchDensity == 1600)$TotalWeight)
# normal, range 0 - 30, peak at 12

#############
##### Distributions are all the same. OK to model together
#############

### NFWF ALL Model ###
## Choose distribution family
TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma <- glmmTMB(TotalWeight ~ 1, 
                      family = Gamma(link = "log"), 
                      data = QuadStats)
TotalWeight_NFWF_gaussian <- glmmTMB(TotalWeight ~ 1, 
                      family = gaussian(link = "identity"), 
                      data = QuadStats)
# Check goodness of fit
simulateResiduals(TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma, n = 1000, plot = T)
simulateResiduals(TotalWeight_NFWF_gaussian, n = 1000, plot = T)
AIC(TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma, TotalWeight_NFWF_gaussian)
## Gamma has good fit and better AIC (deltaAIC = 5)

## Add effects
TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma_CD <- glmmTMB(TotalWeight ~ Treatment, 
                      family = Gamma(link = "log"), 
                      data = QuadStats)
TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma_CDfactor <- glmmTMB(TotalWeight ~ factor(Treatment), 
                      family = Gamma(link = "log"), 
                      data = QuadStats)
TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma_CD_random <- glmmTMB(TotalWeight ~ Treatment + (1 | FixedLocationID), 
                      family = Gamma(link = "log"), 
                      data = QuadStats)
TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma_CDfactor_random <- glmmTMB(TotalWeight ~ factor(Treatment) + (1 | FixedLocationID), # BEST
                      family = Gamma(link = "log"), 
                      data = QuadStats)
TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma_CDfactor_random_var <- glmmTMB(TotalWeight ~ factor(Treatment) + (1 | FixedLocationID), # add varience
                      family = Gamma(link = "log"),
                      dispformula = ~ Treatment,
                      data = QuadStats)
# Check goodness of fit
simulateResiduals(TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma_CD, n = 1000, plot = T)
simulateResiduals(TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma_CDfactor, n = 1000, plot = T)
simulateResiduals(TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma_CD_random, n = 1000, plot = T)
simulateResiduals(TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma_CDfactor_random, n = 1000, plot = T)
simulateResiduals(TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma_CDfactor_random_var, n = 1000, plot = T)
AIC(TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma_CD, TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma_CDfactor, TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma_CD_random, TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma_CDfactor_random, TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma_CDfactor_random_var)
## Adding FixedLocation as a random (not fixed) effect helps and allows us to make larger generalizations; Treating Treatment as a factor doesn't improves fit; adding seperate variance term does not improve fit

# post-hoc test
# 1. Get estimated marginal means (on the original response scale)
em_cultch <- emmeans(TotalWeight_NFWF_gamma_CDfactor_random, ~ factor(Treatment), type = "response")

# 2. Perform pairwise comparisons with a Tukey adjustment
pairwise_comparisons <- pairs(em_cultch, adjust = "tukey")

# View the results
print(em_cultch)
print(pairwise_comparisons)

# Generate Compact Letter Display (CLD)
cld_results <- multcomp::cld(
  em_cultch,
  alpha = 0.05,
  Letters = letters,      # Uses lowercase a, b, ab instead of numbers
  adjust = "tukey",       # Matches your pairwise Tukey adjustment
  sort = FALSE            # Keeps your original treatment order (200 to 3200)
)

# Convert comparisons to a dataframe and display
cld_results %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  kable(digits = 3, 
        caption = "Comparison of Substrate Density Across Different Treatments")

# Convert comparisons to a dataframe and display
pairwise_comparisons %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  kable(digits = 3, 
        caption = "Comparison of Substrate Density Across Different Treatments")

# "Post-hoc pairwise comparisons using Tukey's honest significant difference (HSD) adjustment revealed statistically significant differences in total sample weight among some of the tested treatments. The highest estimated average weight occurred at Low-Relief (Mean = 16.3 [13.6-19.6]), followed by High-Relief (Mean = 14.6 [12.1-17.5]), then Easthole (Mean = 13.9 [9.9-19.5]), then Cat-Point (Mean = 11.0 [7.6-15.8], and finally NFWF-2021 (Mean = 8.1 [6.6-9.9]). 
# All 2024 Treatments were similar (p>0.30); Cat-Point, Easthole, and NFWF-2021 were similar (p>0.06); High & Low-Relief were different from NFWF-2021 (p>0.001)
# These results suggest sample weight increases up to 800; but diminishing results above 800. It may also be that rock size is also contributing to the differences

```

``` {r TotalWeight Models and Dataframes}
###############
### Create model
###############

### NFWF-2024 ALL Model ###
TotalWeight_NFWF <- glmmTMB(TotalWeight ~ factor(Treatment) + (1 | FixedLocationID), # BEST
                      family = Gamma(link = "log"), 
                      data = QuadStats)
# Check goodness of fit & summary
simulateResiduals(TotalWeight_NFWF, n = 1000, plot = T)
summary(TotalWeight_NFWF)


###############
### Create dataframes to store values for plots and tables 
###############

# Generate Modeled Means, CI, and SE
# emmeans needed to extract values of Random effects
TotalWeightStats_Subtidal_modeled <- emmeans(TotalWeight_NFWF, ~ Treatment, type = "response") %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  rename(TotalWeightMean_modeled = response,
         TotalWeightLower_modeled = asymp.LCL,
         TotalWeightUpper_modeled = asymp.UCL) %>%
  mutate(TotalWeightMeanDensity_modeled = round((TotalWeightMean_modeled * 4), 1),
         TotalWeightLowerDensity_modeled = round((TotalWeightLower_modeled * 4), 1),
         TotalWeightUpperDensity_modeled = round((TotalWeightUpper_modeled * 4), 1)) %>%
  select(-df) %>%
  mutate(TotalWeightUpperDensity_modeled = case_when(
    TotalWeightMean_modeled <= 0 ~ 0,
    TRUE ~ TotalWeightUpperDensity_modeled))

# Generate raw mean and SD
TotalWeightStats_Subtidal_RAW <- QuadStats %>%
  group_by(Treatment) %>%
  summarise_ALL() %>%
  arrange(Treatment) %>%
  select(-matches("Num"))

# Combine into single table and remove intermediate dataframes
TotalWeightStats_Subtidal_ALL <- left_join(TotalWeightStats_Subtidal_modeled, 
                              TotalWeightStats_Subtidal_RAW, 
                              by = c("Treatment"))
```

``` {r NumLive Model selection, eval = FALSE}
# nbinom, range 150 - 1000, strong peak at 250;

# Pilot LOW
hist(subset(QuadStats, CultchDensity == 1600)$NumLive)
# normal, range 0 - 1000, peak at 400

#############
##### a variety of distributions, though not strong. Modelling together in order to detect differences
#############

NumLive_NFWF_nbinom <- glmmTMB(NumLive ~ factor(Treatment), 
                 family = nbinom2, 
                 data = QuadStats)
NumLive_NFWF_nbinom_random <- glmmTMB(NumLive ~ factor(Treatment) + (1 | FixedLocationID), 
                 family = nbinom2, 
                 data = QuadStats)
NumLive_NFWF_nbinom_random_disp <- glmmTMB(NumLive ~ factor(Treatment) + (1 | FixedLocationID), # Best
                 family = nbinom2, 
                 dispformula = ~ Treatment,
                 data = QuadStats)
simulateResiduals(NumLive_NFWF_nbinom, n = 1000, plot = T)
simulateResiduals(NumLive_NFWF_nbinom_random, n = 1000, plot = T)
simulateResiduals(NumLive_NFWF_nbinom_random_disp, n = 1000, plot = T)
# Compared 
AIC(NumLive_NFWF_nbinom, NumLive_NFWF_nbinom_random, NumLive_NFWF_nbinom_random_disp)
anova(NumLive_NFWF_nbinom, NumLive_NFWF_nbinom_random, NumLive_NFWF_nbinom_random_disp)
#### Accounting for Treatment, FixedLocationID as a random effect and each Treatment's variance seperately yields the best model, no errors, and lower AIC than the other two models

summary(NumLive_NFWF_nbinom_random_disp)

# post-hoc test
# 1. Get estimated marginal means (on the original response scale)
emm_Live <- emmeans(NumLive_NFWF_nbinom_random_disp, ~ factor(Treatment), type = "response")

# 2. Perform pairwise comparisons with a Tukey adjustment
pairwise_comparisons_live <- pairs(emm_Live, adjust = "tukey")

# View the results
print(emm_Live)
print(pairwise_comparisons_live)

# Generate Compact Letter Display (CLD)
cld_result_live <- multcomp::cld(
  emm_Live,
  alpha = 0.05,
  Letters = letters,      # Uses lowercase a, b, ab instead of numbers
  adjust = "tukey",       # Matches your pairwise Tukey adjustment
  sort = FALSE            # Keeps your original treatment order (200 to 3200)
)

# Convert comparisons to a dataframe and display
cld_result_live %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  kable(digits = 3, 
        caption = "Comparison of NumLive Across Different Treatments")

# Convert comparisons to a dataframe and display
pairwise_comparisons_live %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  kable(digits = 3, 
        caption = "Comparison of NumLive Across Different Treatments")


# "Post-hoc pairwise comparisons using Tukey's honest significant difference (HSD) adjustment revealed statistically significant differences in number of live oysters among some of the tested treatments. The highest estimated average NumLive occurred at High-Relief (Mean = 383 [235-623]), followed by Low-Relief (Mean = 377 [226-631]), then Easthole (Mean = 160 [61-418]), then Cat-Point (Mean = 159 [58-434], and finally NFWF-2021 (Mean = 76 [43-135]). 
# All 2024 Treatments were similar (p>0.23); Cat-Point, Easthole, and NFWF-2021 were similar (p>0.43); High & Low-Relief were different from NFWF-2021 (p>0.001)
# These results suggest NumLive increases up to 800; but diminishing results above 800. 

# "Although a localized mortality event occurred in one 800-density replicate (Easthole) two months prior to sampling, it did not significantly alter final live oyster abundance relative to its companion replicate (\(p = 1.00\)). However, the event significantly altered population structure, resulting in radically different size distributions among survivors (\(p < 0.0001\)). This decoupling of abundance and size highlights that while final numerical carrying capacity may be consistently constrained at lower cultch volumes, the underlying biomass, size-frequency distribution, and structural stability of the reef remain highly sensitive to episodic disturbance events."

```

``` {r DLRatio Model selection, eval = FALSE}
# 1. Estimated Proportion Dead: NumDead / (NumDead + NumLive)

emm_DLRatio_logit <- emmeans(DLRatio_NFWF_betabinomial_disp_T_FLID, ~ Treatment)
dl_summary_DLRatio <- as.data.frame(emm_DLRatio_logit)
dl_summary_DLRatio$dead_live_ratio <- exp(dl_summary_DLRatio$emmean)
dl_summary_DLRatio$ratio_LCL       <- exp(dl_summary_DLRatio$asymp.LCL)
dl_summary_DLRatio$ratio_UCL       <- exp(dl_summary_DLRatio$asymp.UCL)
print(dl_summary_DLRatio[, c("Treatment", "dead_live_ratio", "ratio_LCL", "ratio_UCL")])

# 3. Pairwise Comparisons (outputs odds ratios comparing dead:live between treatments)
pairwise_comparisons_DLRatio <- pairs(emm_DLRatio_prop, adjust = "tukey")

# View the results
print(emm_DLRatio_prop)
print(emm_DLRatio_logit)
print(pairwise_comparisons_DLRatio)

# Generate Compact Letter Display (CLD)
cld_result_DLRatio <- multcomp::cld(
  emm_DLRatio_prop,
  alpha = 0.05,
  Letters = letters,      # Uses lowercase a, b, ab instead of numbers
  adjust = "tukey",       # Matches your pairwise Tukey adjustment
  sort = FALSE            # Keeps your original treatment order (200 to 3200)
)

# Convert comparisons to a dataframe and display
cld_result_DLRatio %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  kable(digits = 3, 
        caption = "Comparison of DLRatio Across Different Treatments")

# Convert comparisons to a dataframe and display
pairwise_comparisons_DLRatio %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  kable(digits = 3, 
        caption = "Comparison of DLRatio Across Different Treatments")


# "Post-hoc pairwise comparisons using Tukey's honest significant difference (HSD) adjustment revealed statistically significant differences in ratio of dead:live oysters among all of the tested treatments. The highest estimated average Dead:live ratio occurred at Easthole (Mean = 0.84 [0.37-1.89]), followed by HNFWF-2021 (Mean = 0.20 [0.12-0.34]), then High-Relief (Mean = 0.12 [0.08-0.18]), then Low-Relief (Mean = 0.09 [0.06-0.13], and finally Cat-Point (Mean = 0.06 [0.03-0.14]). 
# All Treatments except Easthole were similar (p>0.11); Easthole was different from all other treatments (p<0.032)
# These results suggest Easthole had asignificantly higher ratio of Dead:Live oysters, likely due to the observed mortality event there. Dead:Live ratio does not appear to be affected by the treatments  

```

``` {r NumLegal Model selection, eval = FALSE}
# Figure out which data distribution to use

# Pilot LOW

# normal, range 0 - 120, peak at 75

#############
##### a variety of distributions, though not strong. Modelling together in order to detect differences
#############

NumLegal_NFWF_nbinom <- glmmTMB(NumLegal ~ factor(Treatment), 
                 family = nbinom2, 
                 data = QuadStats)
NumLegal_NFWF_nbinom_random <- glmmTMB(NumLegal ~ factor(Treatment) + (1 | FixedLocationID), 
                 family = nbinom2, 
                 data = QuadStats)
NumLegal_NFWF_nbinom_random_disp <- glmmTMB(NumLegal ~ factor(Treatment) + (1 | FixedLocationID), # Best
                 family = nbinom2, 
                 dispformula = ~ Treatment,
                 data = QuadStats)
simulateResiduals(NumLegal_NFWF_nbinom, n = 1000, plot = T)
simulateResiduals(NumLegal_NFWF_nbinom_random, n = 1000, plot = T)
simulateResiduals(NumLegal_NFWF_nbinom_random_disp, n = 1000, plot = T)
# Compared 
AIC(NumLegal_NFWF_nbinom, NumLegal_NFWF_nbinom_random, NumLegal_NFWF_nbinom_random_disp)
anova(NumLegal_NFWF_nbinom, NumLegal_NFWF_nbinom_random, NumLegal_NFWF_nbinom_random_disp)
#### Accounting for Treatment, FixedLocationID as a random effect and each Treatment's variance separately yields the best model, no errors, and lower AIC than the other two models

summary(NumLegal_NFWF_nbinom_random_disp)

# post-hoc test
# 1. Get estimated marginal means (on the original response scale)
emm_NumLegal <- emmeans(NumLegal_NFWF_nbinom_random_disp, ~ factor(Treatment), type = "response")

# 2. Perform pairwise comparisons with a Tukey adjustment
pairwise_comparisons_NumLegal <- pairs(emm_NumLegal, adjust = "tukey")

# View the results
print(emm_NumLegal)
print(pairwise_comparisons_NumLegal)

# Generate Compact Letter Display (CLD)
cld_result_NumLegal <- multcomp::cld(
  emm_NumLegal,
  alpha = 0.05,
  Letters = letters,      # Uses lowercase a, b, ab instead of numbers
  adjust = "tukey",       # Matches your pairwise Tukey adjustment
  sort = FALSE            # Keeps your original treatment order (200 to 3200)
)

# Convert comparisons to a dataframe and display
cld_result_NumLegal %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  kable(digits = 3, 
        caption = "Comparison of NumLegal Across Different Treatments")

# Convert comparisons to a dataframe and display
pairwise_comparisons_NumLegal %>%
  as.data.frame() %>%
  kable(digits = 3, 
        caption = "Comparison of NumLegal Across Different Treatments")


# "Post-hoc pairwise comparisons using Tukey's honest significant difference (HSD) adjustment revealed statistically significant differences in number of legal-sized oysters among some of the tested treatments. The highest estimated average number of legal-sized occurred at Low-Relief (Mean = 46 [20-109]), followed by Cat-Point (Mean = 30 [6-167]), then NFWF-2021 (Mean = 20 [8-55]), then High-Relief (Mean = 16 [7-37], and finally Easthole (Mean = 1 [0-4]). 
# All Treatments except Easthole were similar (p>0.41); Easthole was different from all other treatments (p<0.02)
# These results suggest number of legal-sized oysters on all treatments is highly variable, yet statistically similar. 

# "A localized mortality event occurred in one 800-density replicate (Easthole) two months prior to sampling, it did not significantly alter final live oyster abundance relative to its companion replicate (\(p = 1.00\)). However, the event significantly altered population structure, resulting in radically different size distributions among survivors (\(p < 0.0001\)). This decoupling of abundance and size highlights that while final numerical carrying capacity may be consistently constrained at lower cultch volumes, the underlying biomass, size-frequency distribution, and structural stability of the reef remain highly sensitive to episodic disturbance events."
```
